$comment: App-mirror registry — the ONE list of static hosts that carry the identical dist (see docs/redundancy.md). deploy/emit-matrix.mjs turns this into the GitHub Actions fan-out. Rules: secrets/vars are NAMES only (values live in GitHub repo secrets/vars, never here); deploy.codeChanges must be "none" for every host (relative base './' + hash routes make the same build run anywhere); max 10 entries. status: live | ready | pending-account | dropped (dropped requires dropReason). This committed registry holds SELECTED doors only: 3 live + 7 pending-account. Dropped hosts (GitLab Pages, Vercel, Azure Static Web Apps, Deno Deploy, Codeberg) are NOT registry entries — their rejection reasons live in the host survey in docs/redundancy.md so the survey never has to be repeated blind. Verdicts verified against vendor docs 2026-10-01; additions verified 2026-10-02.

hosts.basePathNote: Served from /drift-shop/ subpath — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Dedicated job in deploy-mirrors.yml using actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages. Gated on vars.MIRROR_GITHUB_PAGES=true until the owner retires the current branch-based deploy (turn both on at once = two deploys racing).

hosts.headersNote: No real response headers on Pages — CSP rides in a <meta> tag; frame-ancestors/HSTS unavailable (accepted, documented).
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Repo Settings -> Pages -> Source: GitHub Actions (only when enabling the workflow job).
hosts.tosNote: IMPORTANT (verified 2026-10-01, docs.github.com pages limits): GitHub Pages is not intended for or allowed to be used as a free web-hosting service to run an online business, e-commerce site, or SaaS. The current live app door sits on GitHub Pages — the plan is to move the COMMERCIAL app's primary door to Cloudflare Pages / Firebase Hosting and keep GitHub Pages for the manual and docs (its intended use). Do not expand commercial reliance on this door.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=$CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT (cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3; the old pages-action is deprecated).

hosts.headersNote: Can send REAL headers via a public/_headers file later; meta CSP works today. Direct Upload project (not git-connected) so the fan-out ships the exact same dist.
hosts.limitsNote: Free: 500 builds/mo; static requests/bandwidth unlimited; 20,000 files/site; 25 MiB max file. Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Done 2026-10-02: Cloudflare account reached via the already signed-in GitHub route (no phone/card/CAPTCHA); Direct Upload Pages project `vendra` created and verified at vendra-1f2.pages.dev. API-token automation (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID + CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT) is still pending for hands-off fan-out.
hosts.signupCheck: Verified live 2026-10-02: Continue with GitHub (staros-builds) reached the dashboard with only read-only email/profile authorization. No phone, card, password, or CAPTCHA was required.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: firebase-tools deploy --only hosting (service-account auth via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS; firebase login:ci tokens are deprecated upstream). Uses firebase.json in this repo (hosting.public=dist).

hosts.headersNote: Real headers are expressible in firebase.json hosting.headers later; meta CSP works today.
hosts.limitsNote: Spark plan (no card): 10 GB hosting storage, 10 GB/month transfer; over-quota sites are disabled until next month. Never upgrade to Blaze (links a billing account + card). Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create Firebase project (Spark plan, no card) under the owner Google account; create a service account with the Firebase Hosting Admin role, download its JSON key into the FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT repo secret; repo var FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID.
hosts.signupCheck: Uses a Google account. Pick an existing Google account under Jesse's control. Firebase itself asks for no card on Spark. Do NOT create a brand-new Google account for this unless needed: Google may ask for phone verification when creating one — Jesse completes that step himself if it appears.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: npx surge@0.40 dist $SURGE_DOMAIN (0.40 grammar requires the domain argument — we always pass it).

hosts.headersNote: No custom response headers; meta CSP carries the policy.
hosts.limitsNote: No published bandwidth/storage quota — treat as unquantified fair-use risk, not a hard number. Custom domains + certs free for everyone (0.40 release notes). Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: surge signup with the owner email (no card); surge token; repo var SURGE_DOMAIN=<name>.surge.sh; secrets SURGE_LOGIN + SURGE_TOKEN.
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password from the command line (surge login). Historically one of the lowest-friction signups — no phone, no card, no known challenge gauntlet.

hosts.limitsNote: CAUTION — Hobby workspace: 5 GB/month outbound bandwidth (cut from 100 GB in Apr 2026), 500 pipeline (build) minutes/mo. Without a card on file, exhausting bandwidth suspends Free services until next month. Secondary door only. Verified 2026-10-01.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job pushes the built dist/ contents to the root of the <workspace>.bitbucket.io repository's main branch over HTTPS with a repository access token (BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN). Byte-identical by construction (a plain git push of artifacts).

hosts.headersNote: No custom response headers; meta CSP carries the policy.
hosts.limitsNote: Free workspace plan; one static site per workspace, served from the repo named exactly <workspace>.bitbucket.io. Atlassian publishes no bandwidth quota for these sites — treat as unquantified fair-use. The site is public even if the repo is private (fine: the app shell is public; all data lives behind Supabase RLS). Verified 2026-10-02 (Atlassian Support, Publishing a website on Bitbucket Cloud).
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create the Atlassian/Bitbucket account (project inbox + CAPTCHA; read the confirmation in the inbox); create workspace `vendra` if free (lowercase, DNS-clean); create a private repo named exactly vendra.bitbucket.io; add a repository access token as BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN and the workspace id as repo var BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE. Add https://<workspace>.bitbucket.io/** to the Supabase Auth redirect allowlist before announcing.
hosts.signupCheck: Atlassian account = email + password with a CAPTCHA and an email confirmation. No phone, no card. If Atlassian bot checks escalate on the flagged network, Jesse completes the CAPTCHA once.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job pushes the built dist/ contents to the staros-builds/staros-builds.github.io repository over SSH with a dedicated deploy key (ROOT_SITE_DEPLOY_KEY); Pages serves that repo at the account root. Deliberately NOT the github-pages deploy type: door #1 (drift-shop project site) keeps its own gated Actions deploy.

hosts.headersNote: No real response headers on Pages — CSP rides in a <meta> tag; frame-ancestors/HSTS unavailable (accepted, documented).
hosts.limitsNote: Existing GitHub Pages entitlement: 1 GB site, ~100 GB/month soft bandwidth (GitHub Pages limits, verified 2026-10-02). Same provider as door #1 — counts toward the 10 addresses, NOT toward provider diversity.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create the public repo staros-builds/staros-builds.github.io if it does not exist; add a write deploy key and store the private half as ROOT_SITE_DEPLOY_KEY. If the app itself is ever mounted here (rather than the landing page), add https://staros-builds.github.io/** to the Supabase Auth redirect allowlist first.
hosts.tosNote: Same GitHub Pages terms as door #1: Pages is not for running an online business / e-commerce / SaaS. This door's job is the front door (landing page + manual links into the commercial doors), not a checkout-bearing app door.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job uploads the built dist/ file-by-file with the Neocities API (POST https://neocities.org/api/upload, bearer NEOCITIES_API_KEY), then the release verifies the remote file list and /build.json hash (free accounts restrict some upload file types; the current dist uses only ordinary web types).

hosts.headersNote: CONDITIONAL: Neocities lists 'Less Strict Content Security Policy' as a paid Supporter perk, implying free sites get a stricter host-set CSP. On first deploy, fetch the live response headers; if the host CSP blocks connections to the Supabase origin, demote this door to landing/manual duty before announcing. No ads or wrappers either way.
hosts.limitsNote: Free: 1 GB storage, 200 GB/month bandwidth, site subdomain with SSL; Neocities never puts advertising on sites. Custom domains/WebDAV/multiple sites are Supporter-only ($5/mo — never buy). One site per free account. Verified 2026-10-02 (neocities.org/supporter).
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create the account (project inbox + simple CAPTCHA + confirmation link read in the inbox); claim the site name (try `vendra` first); copy the API key from Settings -> API into the NEOCITIES_API_KEY repo secret (never paste it in chat). After the CSP header check passes, add https://<site>.neocities.org/** to the Supabase Auth redirect allowlist before announcing.
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password + a simple CAPTCHA, plus an email confirmation link. No phone, no card. If signup is refused from the flagged network, Jesse completes it once by hand.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root on the assigned edge URL — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Dashboard-wired (external): Sevalla builds from the connected GitHub repo itself (build: npm run build, publish: dist, env VITE_SUPABASE_URL + VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY). No repo secret exists yet and no hook/API is wired; the release pipeline's /build.json hash check gates any announcement, so a drifted rebuild is caught before the door is advertised.

hosts.headersNote: Check the assigned edge URL's response headers at setup (note any X-Robots-Tag, which does not break the app but must be known before the address is advertised).
hosts.limitsNote: Static sites $0 tier: 100 sites, 600 build minutes/month, 100 GB bandwidth/month/account, 1 GB per site (kinsta.com/static-site-hosting, now presented as Sevalla; verified 2026-10-02). Brand migration (Kinsta -> Sevalla) is recent — quotas and even the product name may move again; re-verify the free tier at setup time.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Sign up (GitHub OAuth on the signed-in session if offered, else project inbox); STOP if a card is requested — that would contradict the $0 product page and demote this host. Connect staros-builds/drift-shop with the build settings in the mechanism note; record the exact assigned edge URL here and check its headers; add that origin to the Supabase Auth redirect allowlist before announcing.
hosts.signupCheck: Email or Google/GitHub SSO; no card for static sites (the $0 tier is a product, not a trial). If the flow asks for a card, stop and report — that demotes this host to rejected.
